title: San Jose
name: San Jose
metaTitle: 1031 Exchange Advisory in San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange advisory for San Jose owners of downtown office, North San Jose tech campuses, and airport-adjacent industrial, with facilities-level diligence on each.

sections.html: San Jose is the largest city in the Bay Area by population, and its commercial stock spans a downtown office core still working through its own vacancy recovery, sprawling North San Jose technology campuses, and airport-adjacent industrial product near Mineta San Jose International. An exchange buyer here should not assume the downtown vacancy headlines that dominate coverage of the submarket apply evenly across all three categories, since each answers to a different tenant base with its own facilities demands.

sections.heading: Three Distinct San Jose Markets Under One City Name
sections.html: Downtown San Jose's office towers have dealt with vacancy pressure of their own, though generally on a smaller scale and lower price basis than comparable San Francisco Financial District product, and the ongoing Diridon Station-area development has kept long-term redevelopment interest active even where near-term leasing remains soft. North San Jose, running along the 101 and 880 corridors, holds large campus-style buildings leased to major technology employers including a long-standing Cisco presence, generally on bigger floor plates and lower per-square-foot pricing than downtown. Airport-adjacent industrial and flex space near Mineta San Jose International serves logistics and light manufacturing tenants who value the access more than any downtown proximity.

sections.heading: The Facilities Checklist That Applies Across San Jose's Office Stock
sections.html:
Before recommending a San Jose office candidate, whether downtown or in North San Jose, we ask the facilities contact to confirm:

  • elevator and mechanical system age relative to the building's construction era
  • floor-by-floor electrical capacity for whatever tenant profile the seller is marketing to
  • parking ratio adequacy, which varies significantly between downtown high-rise product and North San Jose's lower-density campuses
  • security staffing and after-hours access protocols, particularly relevant for downtown towers with partial vacancy
  • light rail or transit access impact on tenant demand where applicable

sections.heading: Downtown Redevelopment Interest Should Not Replace Current Income Underwriting
sections.html: Diridon Station-area development plans have drawn real long-term interest to parts of downtown San Jose, and that interest can push asking prices above what current in-place office income actually supports. A buyer identifying a downtown candidate under 45-day pressure should underwrite the building on its existing lease roll first and treat any redevelopment upside as a bonus rather than the basis for the offer, since large-scale mixed-use development timelines run on a much longer clock than an exchange investor's replacement deadline, and treating a redevelopment story as guaranteed income is one of the more common mistakes we see brought to us after closing.

sections.heading: Tenant Coordination Differs Sharply Between Downtown and North San Jose
sections.html: A downtown San Jose office tower with partial vacancy requires the same kind of active facilities coordination around security staffing and mechanical balancing that a similarly situated Financial District building would, since dark floors affect operating costs and life-safety planning either way. North San Jose's larger campus tenants, by contrast, often coordinate more directly with a facilities manager on move logistics tied to a single large lease, with less day-to-day churn but higher stakes if that tenant's needs change. Airport-adjacent industrial tenants operate on yet another rhythm, driven by loading dock scheduling and truck circulation rather than office-style tenant improvement cycles, and a facilities manager working across that category should not be judged against an office-building benchmark that simply does not apply to their day-to-day responsibilities.

sections.heading: Underwriting the Real Cost of San Jose's Varied Stock
sections.html:
A downtown San Jose office tower generally needs the same mechanical and elevator capital planning as an aging Financial District building, and a buyer should not assume the lower price basis here means lower near-term capital needs. North San Jose campus product and airport-adjacent industrial space vary more building to building, and a direct engineering review of each specific candidate should replace any assumption based on the broader submarket's reputation.

A facilities manager who has worked across more than one of these San Jose categories can usually explain why two buildings with similar asking rents carry very different real carrying costs, since a downtown tower's elevator bank and a North San Jose campus's data center cooling load have almost nothing in common as capital items. An exchange buyer should treat that person's input as seriously as a leasing broker's opinion of value, particularly when working against a tight 45-day identification window.

faqs.q: Does downtown San Jose office vacancy make it a weak choice for a 1031 replacement?
faqs.a: It depends on the specific building's lease roll and mechanical condition, not the submarket label. Underwrite current in-place income first and treat any Diridon Station-area redevelopment upside as a bonus rather than the basis for the offer.

faqs.q: How is North San Jose different from downtown for a commercial investor?
faqs.a: North San Jose holds larger campus-style buildings on bigger floor plates, generally leased to major technology tenants at a lower per-square-foot price than downtown high-rise product.

faqs.q: What should be checked before identifying a San Jose office candidate?
faqs.a: Elevator and mechanical system age, floor-by-floor electrical capacity, parking ratio, and security staffing levels, particularly for downtown towers carrying partial vacancy.

faqs.q: How does tenant coordination differ between downtown San Jose and North San Jose campuses?
faqs.a: Downtown towers with partial vacancy need active coordination around security and mechanical balancing, while North San Jose's larger single-tenant campuses see less frequent turnover but higher stakes tied to one lease decision.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange San Francisco confirm my San Jose property qualifies for exchange treatment?
faqs.a: No. We coordinate planning, property identification, and communication among an investor's advisors. Qualification is determined by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
